summary.headline: FY26 revenue rose 23.1% to INR3,104.1 million, but blended EBITDA margin fell to 31.7% and FY26 PAT grew only 1.4%.
summary.overview: Suraksha Diagnostic closed FY26 with revenue from operations of INR3,104.1 million (up 23.1%) and FY26 EBITDA of about INR985-986 million, with margin down from 33.8% to 31.8%. Q4 FY26 revenue was INR822 million (up 25%) with EBITDA of INR252 million at a 31% margin, flat year on year. Q4 PAT margin fell to 7.6% from 11% on higher depreciation, finance cost and tax. The company added 2 hubs, 11 spokes and 3 PPP centres in FY26, taking the count to 68, and management guided to a sharp margin dip in FY27 from new-centre pre-operative costs. Patient growth in Q4 slowed to low single digits, which management attributed to seasonality and to a patient-ID metric it said is unreliable.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at around 15%, which management said it does not mind over-delivering.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided to stabilise at about 33% (one answer said about 37%, which conflicts with the 33% guidance given elsewhere on the call); mid-term about 35%, long-term about 38-39%.
FY27 growth: mature centres contribute about 9%; the balance comes from newly added centres.
FY27 capex for five hubs and eight spokes is about INR70 crore; two centres delayed from FY26 have already had most of their capex incurred.
Centre count: 68 in FY26, with 14 more planned for FY27 (82 total) and about 100 by FY28 per the analyst's summary, which management confirmed.
Centres opened since listing should turn margin-positive in about six months, but new openings will dilute margin.

qa_highlights.question: Was the election a factor in Q4 and in the centre additions?
qa_highlights.answer: Some planned centres were delayed by licences and power; of the four centres guided for Q3, two opened and two were to open in May 2026. About 75 centres were originally planned, and the company confirmed it aims for 100 by FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margin recover to 34-35%?
qa_highlights.answer: Mature centres run at 36-37%; management expects a mid-term stabilisation at 35% and long-term 38-39%, while new-centre additions keep diluting margin near term.

qa_highlights.question: Expected FY27 growth and mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue growth about 15%; mature centres add about 9% of growth, with the rest from new centres. Radiology and pathology mix to track industry norms of about 55:45.

qa_highlights.question: Why did patient growth slow in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited seasonality (winter fizzles out by March) and higher-value infection tests. Management said patient count is a flawed metric because of duplicate patient records and does not track it closely.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin decline from 33.8% to 31.8%?
qa_highlights.answer: Fixed costs for new centres rose, with pre-operative and rental costs; management did not quantify the drag.

qa_highlights.question: What is the professional fee line and why is it large?
qa_highlights.answer: Professional fees cover radiologists, pathologists and OPD doctor consultation; they are variable, with doctors paid 85% of consultation fees. Analyst cited the line at about 16-17% of revenue.

risks_watch: Margin dilution from continued new-centre openings: FY27 guidance of about 33% versus 31.8% in FY26 and 36-37% at mature centres.
Patient volume growth slowed sharply in Q4 and management declined to track patient numbers, limiting visibility on volume.
Pre-Ind AS figures were quoted inconsistently (INR53 crore vs INR75 crore EBITDA, and PAT INR53 crore vs INR39 crore), so reconciliation is needed.
Execution risk on multi-state expansion into Bihar, Tripura and Jharkhand, and on centre timing given licence and power delays.
Rising depreciation and finance cost squeezed Q4 PAT margin to 7.6%; FY26 PAT grew only 1.4%.
Some follow-ups were promised but not answered (pre-operative cost split, MRI/CT utilisation, doctor-consultant revenue step-up).
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term expansion and margin potential, but cautious on near-term margins, which management attributed to new-centre ramp-up. Evasive on patient volume metrics, modality utilisation and the pre-operative cost split, where it deferred answers.
key_quotes: The gap between our mature margins and blended margins represents a clear runway for future profitability as our newer regional hubs scale up to full maturity.
